continuous-raster-visualization

A Claude Skill that renders single-band, continuous-value GeoTIFF rasters into publication-style map figures for remote sensing work — LST, NDVI, IRECI, TRVI, AGC, and similar outputs.

Demo output

Land Surface Temperature, Kalimantan 2025 — percentile stretch, lst_classic palette, left-aligned title, English labels (all current defaults).

Built-in palettes

LST classic

lst_classic

water_index

ndvi_custom

YlGn

Spectral

Feature overview

  • Stretch: min-max, percentile (default 2-98%), or manual vmin/vmax
  • Colorbar endpoints always show the real data min/max, never rounded placeholders
  • Colorbar orientation (vertical/horizontal), label position (side/top), and tick count
  • Coordinate tick format for geographic rasters: DMS, DD, or plain decimal
  • Gridlines on or off
  • Font family (serif/sans-serif) with independent title and subtitle sizes
  • Title/subtitle spacing and alignment (left by default, or center)
  • Output language for default labels: English or Bahasa Indonesia

Tech stack

Python 3.10+ matplotlib rasterio numpy

Quick start

python3 scripts/raster_viz.py INPUT.tif OUTPUT.png \
    --stretch percentile --pmin 2 --pmax 98 \
    --cmap lst_classic \
    --colorbar-orient vertical --colorbar-label "LST (deg C)" \
    --coord-format DD --gridlines \
    --font sans-serif \
    --title "Land Surface Temperature" --subtitle "Kalimantan, 2025"
